text:
The Penguins are home after a three-game trip, and the conversation around them has turned to who might leave. Pierre LeBrun reported Carolina's interest in Erik Karlsson, columns are asking what happens to Evgeni Malkin, and Mark Madden wondered aloud whether the unthinkable is thinkable for Sidney Crosby. That's what 16 points in 19 games does, and our playoff odds of 19% explain why the talk isn't going away. Bryan Rust is on injured reserve (ESPN estimates Dec. 5), and Malkin has moved into his spot beside Crosby and Rickard Rakell.

The problem is less the skaters than the net. Pittsburgh has 52% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), level with Ottawa, but has allowed 3.47 goals a game. Arturs Silovs, our projected starter, is at .855 and 3.6 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. Sergei Murashov won the shootout in San Jose this week and drew good reviews.

Ottawa has its own scar from this week. Nick Cousins was knocked out by Jakob Chychrun's hit on Tuesday, a hit the league deemed legal, per ESPN, and he's out 7 to 10 days. William Eklund is out until January with an ankle injury, and Tim Stützle has moved onto his line with Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund. The Senators still won Thursday, coming back in the third to beat Colorado in overtime on Shane Pinto's birthday goal. Samuel Ersson starts at -1.1 on the season; Coming Down the Pipe reported Linus Ullmark still wasn't at Thursday's morning skate.

Philip Tomasino plays in Pittsburgh for the first time since leaving the Penguins, one point from 100 career points. Zetterlund is one of our Sleepers at 19% to score. Stützle leads Ottawa at 35%; Crosby leads Pittsburgh at 34%. Ottawa takes 4.7 penalties a game, which hands a Penguins power play with Crosby and Rakell on it plenty of looks. Our playoff odds for the Senators: 77%.
headline: Penguins come home to the sell-off talk
